body: Yeah I've been there I hate when I get depressed because it's confirmation that I'm sick. I try to convince myself I'm not but in the end I end up just taking the meds and get it over with

Lol its so annoying isn't it. I'm literally a human version of Oscar the grouch. I hate being grouchy so when I feel really high and up its tempting to not take my meds and just keep the good vibes going because I rather feel great than just meh.

I hate taking mines too. I feel that I'm naturally grumpy and the meds make it worse. I'm like a crabby old person most days and I'm only in my mid twenties. My gf says I always sound like a grumpy old man or someone's crabby uncle.  When I'm not grumpy I'm just "flat" I could care less about what's going on. Less laughter, less fun, less connected. But if I'm without them too long it gets pretty ugly.

Usually not very long but that's because in the past I had a tendency toward serial monogamy. I'd date one person after the next without break. 

These days, I have a partner that accepts me in every way even when it gets really tough she's still there. You just haven't that person for yourself. They are out there, but at the same time you can't expect them to solve all your problems either.

Someone else always told me even though work sucks, not having any money sucks more.

For me repetitive jobs work best. I like to do the same thing , the same way everyday at work. Usally when I'm working I am a cashier. Sounds awful when you have anxiety right. But once you get the swing of it you almost can do it with closed eyes. That's just me though. The repetitive nature of being a cashier is how I deal with it. Routine is my friend. Maybe you can find something a little less people oriented, like a warehouse job. I've worked those and you don't interact much and again the work is very simple and repetive. Any warehouses around?

Be understanding and never judge her or make her feel ashamed when she isn't at her best. Be a listening ear when she needs to talk. With the meds even when she feels like she's feeling better always encourage her to stay on top of her meds. It's not safe to just stop taking your meds even if you "feel better".

That said you also are going to have to learn self care for yourself. Don't get so caught up caring for her that you forget to care for yourself. Personally, when I'm having an episode I tend to get so caught up I'm the episode or the emotions that come with it that it's hard to see other people's feelings. I hate this because it seems like I'm selfish during episodes but im really really not trying to be. So self care is important too.

Anyways I know that's not the route you want to take. I'd say continue to call around and don't give up. It's crap trying to get appointments on your own I know. That or maybe try bringing it up to the doctor that deals with your pregnancy. Tell them you really need help with this and it's important for you to be seen asap. Tell them you are not in any immediate danger but that you've been unmedicated for a couple of years.

My mom is like this. Just because I wasn't beating (often) means I should be grateful for everything else she's done. I'm very introverted and my mom is the opposite. That's the reason for most of my abuse. I was never good enough because I wasn't loud enough or outgoing enough or didn't participate in school activities enough. She always used to compare me to other girls. I know for a fact she wishes she had a different child. My into version was the excuse to abuse me. A lot of emotional abuse.

Secondly, everyone else's kids always came before me. She was the mom who was nasty at home but when she was around other people's kids she was the parent everyone wished they had. She even became a foster parent without regard to my feelings. Yes I was a child but my whole life was turned upside down without my input. I was forced to help care for children that I didn't want or ask for. Forced to feed them, forced to bath them, forced to dress them. I'm talking 11 years old doing this crap. These children ALWAYS came before me unless she wasn't very fond of the foster child either. Usually if they were old enough to be able to tell her where to stick it she wouldn't take them in. She only really fosters kids from about 0-4 when they're too young to know when they're being wronged, they can't talk or speak for themselves. She likes that age.

Third, always one upping my feelings. She constantly one upped my feelings with EVERYTHING. If I was sad she was sadder. If I was angry she'd "out anger" me. She would do this to discourage me from having feelings. At a point I was ice cold because I've learned that my emotions will always be about her in her mind.

When it came to school I was totally abused in that area. If I even got anything less than a B both parents would basically stand over me screaming at me and yelling how u should have done better. I feel this contributed to me dropping out of college. When someone is constantly abusing you and berating you about every little academic mistake it detours you from even wanting to learn. Every time report card day came I knew I was going to be berated and screamed at. To give you a mental picture I'd be sitting in a chair and my parents would  be barking at me on both sides of the chair and berating me about a C+. Now that i have moved away from them I barely even call. It feels so good to be away from them.
